$comment: GOLDEN VECTORS — decisions/0026's conformance suite, finally existing.
0026 said, in the present tense, 'Every platform runs the same vectors; any platform failing any
vector fails CI'. No vectors existed. This file is the first of them, and it starts here because
iOS reported the concrete gap: their decisions/0027 fallback case HAS NEVER EXECUTED. No server
has ever sent an unrecognised enum, so `.unrecognised` decoding, `.rawValue` on it, and the
`gameLabel(game.rawValue) ?? "Pokémon"` fallback are all unexercised — and that last one would
label a ninth game 'Pokémon'.
These vectors need no server change and no ninth game to exist. That is the point: the failure
is reachable from a fixture today, and every platform can be made to face it now rather than
on the morning a ninth game ships.
THE ASSERTION IS ROUND-TRIP EQUALITY, chosen because it is the same check in three languages
with no path DSL and no per-language expectation table. Decode the payload, re-encode it, and
compare. One assertion proves three things at once: it decoded rather than threw (0027 item 1),
the unrecognised value survived rather than being dropped (item 2a), and nothing else in the
object was lost on the way.
EVERY VECTOR DECODES THROUGH ITS CONTAINING RESPONSE TYPE, never the enum alone. The failure
being guarded is a decode error PROPAGATING from a field to the whole object; a fixture that
decoded the enum directly would pass and prove nothing about the path that actually breaks.
2026-09-02 — DISCRIMINATED UNIONS. The vectors below with type EbayPublishErrorResponse cover
the union added when z.discriminatedUnion became emittable. The same asymmetry applies and for
the same reason: the server must refuse to EMIT an error variant it does not know, and the
clients must survive RECEIVING one, because eBay's upstream error codes are an open set we do
not control. A client that hard-failed on a new eBay code would turn 'eBay said something new'
into 'the app broke' at the exact moment a seller is trying to list.
THE MISSING-DISCRIMINATOR VECTOR IS A PARITY VECTOR, not a forward-compatibility one. Swift's
generated decoder used `decode` and Kotlin's degraded to Unknown(""), so the two platforms
disagreed about a malformed body — Swift failing the whole response, Kotlin surfacing an
unknown error. Both now degrade. Without a vector, that divergence is invisible until a
malformed body reaches one platform in production.
TWO CLASSES OF VECTOR, distinguished by `serverAccepts`. The original class is a value the
server must REFUSE to emit (an unknown enum, an unknown union arm) — the stale-fixture guard
depends on that refusal. The second class, `serverAccepts: true`, is a payload the server
legitimately accepts and the clients must also survive: an ADDITIVE field on a known variant.
Zod strips unknown keys rather than rejecting them, so asserting rejection there would have
been asserting the opposite of the design. The field is explicit because a vector whose class
is inferred is a vector whose class can silently change.
⚠️ A LIMIT OF FORWARD COMPATIBILITY, found by the round-trip assertion failing on the additive
vector and worth stating rather than working around. An unknown ENUM VALUE round-trips: the
generated enum keeps the raw string on its unrecognised case. An unknown FIELD on a KNOWN arm
does NOT: it decodes fine and is then DROPPED on re-encode, because the arm is a typed struct
and a typed struct has nowhere to keep it. Making it survive would mean modelling every
generated type as a dictionary-with-extras, which costs the type safety these contracts exist
for. So the round-trip assertion runs on the refuse-class vectors only, and the accept-class
vectors assert decode-and-arm instead. The practical consequence: a client must never decode a
payload and re-send it as its own — it would silently strip fields a newer server added.
The EbayPublishErrorResponse vectors carry `error` (a plain string) alongside `failure` (the
union). That is not redundancy in the fixture — it is the wire shape. Three web screens render
`data.error` directly into a toast, so promoting it to an object would have shown a seller
'[object Object]' mid-publish. The union is additive; the string stays.

vectors.name: ninth_game_in_catalogue_lookup
vectors.why: A game this build has never heard of. The scenario 0027 was written for, and the one that would label a ninth game 'Pokémon' on iOS.

vectors.name: ninth_game_in_one_candidate_only
vectors.why: The shape that bites hardest: a list where most entries are fine. A propagating throw loses the GOOD candidates too, so the picker shows nothing rather than showing fewer.

vectors.name: unknown_confidence_in_catalogue_lookup
vectors.why: Not just GameId — 0027 item 4 covers EVERY generated enum, and confidence is one. Picked deliberately over a made-up field: an unrecognised value has to be exercised on a real enum, or the vector proves nothing about the generated code.

vectors.name: unknown_ebay_error_code
vectors.why: An eBay error code this build has never seen. eBay's codes are an OPEN set arriving from upstream, so this is not hypothetical — it is what next month looks like, and a hard failure here would break listing at the moment a seller is trying to sell.

vectors.name: known_ebay_error_with_extra_field
vectors.why: A KNOWN variant carrying a field this build does not know about. Proves the union does not reject a recognised arm just because a newer server added data to it — additive server changes must not break clients.

vectors.name: ebay_error_missing_discriminator
vectors.why: A malformed error body with NO code field. A PARITY vector, not a forward-compat one: Swift threw and Kotlin degraded, so the platforms disagreed about the same malformed input. Both must degrade to the unknown case rather than one taking down the whole response.

vectors.name: unknown_listing_refusal_reason
vectors.why: A refusal reason added next year (say `quarantined`). The reason list is closed on the server and open on every client: a seller trying to publish must still see a refusal, not a decode error that loses the whole response, and the client must read an unrecognised reason as NOT listable.

vectors.name: unknown_physical_card_status_in_listing_preview
vectors.why: A lifecycle status added after this build (the last two, UNMATCHED and HELD, were exactly this). It sits inside a list of copies, so a propagating throw would lose every OTHER copy in the review table as well as this one.

vectors.name: unknown_game_availability_in_games_response
vectors.why: A third availability state (say `beta`). The list drives which games a seller can choose, so a hard failure would blank the whole game list; a client must read an unrecognised availability as `coming`, never as available.

vectors.name: unknown_unknown_reason_on_a_priced_line
vectors.why: A new reason a figure is null (say `awaiting_review`), on one line of a breakdown. The other lines must still render, and the client must show NO figure for the line rather than a number or a zero.
